We need to discuss the paradox: If every part of a ship is replaced one by one, is it the same ship? The identity problem. The contradictions: identity over time vs. persistence of parts. Solutions: mereology, four-dimensionalism, perdurantism vs. endurantism, essentialism, psychological continuity, definition of identity, conventionalism, fuzzy logic, etc.

We can talk about modern philosophers like David Lewis (modal realism), Peter van Inwagen (metaphysical composition), Peter Strawson (descriptive metaphysics), David Wiggins (sameness of sortal), E.J. Lowe, etc. Also talk about the concept of "ship" as a sortal term, and the role of functions and continuity of form. Also talk about the "paradox" being not a true logical paradox but a conceptual puzzle about identity criteria.

We can discuss possible solutions: (1) Accept that identity is not preserved; it's a new ship. (2) Accept that identity is preserved if the form and function remain unchanged, even if all parts replaced. (3) Use four-dimensionalism: the ship is a spacetime worm; the ship at each time is a temporal part; identity across time is about continuity of the whole entity; the parts can change but the whole persists. (4) Use essentialism: certain parts are essential (e.g., the hull's shape) and if those are preserved, identity holds. (5) Use conventionalism: identity is a matter of social convention; we decide when the ship is the same. (6) Use mereological essentialism: the whole is essential to each part; but that seems contradictory. (7) Use fuzzy logic: identity can be partial.
